probes.assumption: Dust strength decreases by exactly 1 per block of distance from the source.

probes.name: torch_drives_adjacent_dust
probes.assumption: A lit torch drives directly-touching dust to full strength (15). (Only the side direction could be probed this way: dust needs a full support block directly beneath it, and a standing torch does not provide one, so dust cannot physically rest in the one cell directly above a torch -- confirmed live, the block silently fails to place there at all.)

checks.question: dust beside a lit torch reads power=15

probes.name: torch_inverts_when_its_support_is_genuinely_powered
probes.assumption: A torch inverts (goes dark) when the block it is attached to becomes powered by something else, and relights when that power is removed. This is the entire reason a torch can act as a NOT gate.

checks.question: baseline: torch's own dust reads power=15 (support unpowered)
feed dust (touching B) is powered
torch inverts off once its support is genuinely powered
the torch's own dust reading drops to 0 once it is off

probes.name: torch_does_not_power_its_own_support
probes.assumption: A torch does not power the block it is attached to -- if it did, a torch tower would feed itself and turn into a latch instead of an inverter. Mirrored pair on the same shared block: with only the standing torch touching it, a second (wall) torch on another face must stay lit; with a genuine external source also touching it (mediated through dust, the one shape confirmed to relay through a plain block), the same wall torch must invert off -- proving the sensor would have caught it if the rule were false. (A plain second dust cell will not do as the sensor here: dust-mediation was found to reach an *attached component* like a torch, but not a second, merely adjacent piece of dust -- see harness.py.)

checks.question: negative control: the wall torch on B's other face stays lit (standing torch alone)
positive control: the wall torch inverts off once B is genuinely externally powered

probes.name: wall_torch_facing_names_the_attached_block
probes.assumption: A wall torch's `facing` records the direction its head points; it is attached to the block on the *opposite* side (`facing.opposite()`). Mirrored pair: a facing=east torch sandwiched between two stone blocks (west and east) inverts when the west one is genuinely powered, and stays lit when the east one is.

checks.question: lane A: dust feed (touching the west stone) is powered
lane A: torch inverts off when the WEST stone is powered
lane B: dust feed (touching the east stone) is powered
lane B: torch stays lit when the EAST stone is powered (not its attachment)

probes.name: repeater_facing_names_the_input_side
probes.assumption: `facing` names the direction from the repeater's output side to its input side (input = facing, output = facing.opposite()). Mirrored pair: with a source fixed to the west and a dust reader fixed to the east, only facing=west (input=west, matching the source) should light the reader; facing=east should not.
probes.source: src/redstone/simulator/component.rs: repeater_input_position (`pos.offset(facing)`), cites Minecraft Wiki: "facing: the direction from the output side to the input side of a repeater"

checks.question: facing=east (input on the far side from the source) stays dark
facing=west (input on the source side) lights the output

probes.name: comparator_compare_mode_passes_rear_signal
probes.assumption: In compare mode, with the side unpowered, the comparator passes its rear signal through unchanged (here: rear=9 via a 7-long dust chain).

probes.name: comparator_subtract_mode_with_unpowered_side
probes.assumption: In subtract mode with the side unpowered (0), output = rear - 0 = rear -- the same passthrough value as compare mode. (Subtracting an actual non-zero side value could not be independently verified: the side reads whether a *neighbouring block* is itself powered, which is inherently a second hop through a plain block -- the one shape confirmed to never propagate via `/setblock`; see harness.py.)
probes.source: src/redstone/simulator/component.rs: comparator_output, `rear.saturating_sub(side)` in the subtract-mode branch

probes.name: lamp_lights_from_weak_power

probes.name: lamp_on_off_delay
probes.assumption: Our simulator applies the same delay (2 game ticks) symmetrically both turning on and turning off, as a documented simplification. Real Minecraft lights a lamp immediately and only delays turning it off by one redstone tick (2 game ticks), to avoid flicker.
probes.source: src/redstone/simulator/component.rs: LAMP_DELAY_GAME_TICKS and its doc comment, which states this asymmetry explicitly and why the simulator does not replicate it

measurements.question: delay from power applied to lamp lit ("on" delay)
measurements.note: our code assumes ~2 ticks; vanilla is documented as ~0 (instant)

measurements.question: delay from power removed to lamp dark ("off" delay)
measurements.note: our code and vanilla both expect ~2 ticks
